items.title: Authorization Drift in LLM Agents: Evaluating Boundary Compliance in Multi-Step Tool Use
items.snippet: LLM agents can exceed their authorization boundaries while pursuing user goals without an adversary. We formalize this phenomenon as authorization drift across data, tool, scope, and time, and introduce the Authorization Drift Benchmark (ADB): 648 samples across seven domains, each pairing a sufficient compliant path with an attractive unauthorized shortcut. To ensure executable tasks, tempting shortcuts, and feasible compliant paths, Staged Execution-Reflective Synthesis (SERS) grounds benchmark validation in real agent rollouts rather than LLM self-critique. Across 13 LLMs and three frameworks (25,207 trajectories), greater capability accompanies greater drift, with frontier-capable models
items.title_ar: Authorization Drift في LLM agents وأثره على حدود الصلاحيات
items.summary_ar: تعرّف الورقة ظاهرة Authorization Drift حين يتجاوز LLM agents حدود صلاحياتهم أثناء سعيهم لتحقيق أهداف المستخدم دون وجود مهاجم. تقدم الورقة Authorization Drift Benchmark بـ648 عينة عبر سبعة مجالات، وتقيّم 13 LLM عبر ثلاثة frameworks باستخدام 25,207 trajectories. النتيجة الأساسية أن القدرة الأعلى ترافقها انحرافات أكبر.
items.why_ar: وكلاء AI في البنك يحتاجون ضبطاً دقيقاً لصلاحيات الأدوات والبيانات، والـ benchmark يمكن تجربته على agents داخلية.
items.title_en: Authorization Drift in LLM agents: boundary compliance in multi-step tool use
items.summary_en: The paper defines authorization drift, where LLM agents exceed permitted boundaries while pursuing user goals without an adversary. It introduces the 648-sample Authorization Drift Benchmark across seven domains, evaluated on 13 LLMs and three frameworks with 25,207 trajectories. Greater capability is associated with greater drift.
items.why_en: Agents deployed in a bank need strict permission boundaries, and this benchmark can be used to test internal agents.

items.title: AutoCompress: Automated Hardware-Guided Model Compression
items.snippet: LLM pruning must preserve quality while meeting hardware- and workload-specific constraints on latency, throughput, and memory. Existing pruning workflows often target parameter counts, requiring practitioners to manually select model sizes that meet latency, throughput, and GPU memory limits. However, parameter count alone does not predict these metrics, which depend on the model architecture, workload, hardware, and serving engine. We introduce AutoCompress, a hardware-guided compression framework that directly incorporates such constraints into differentiable architecture search. AutoCompress jointly optimizes global and per-layer structure to produce heterogeneous architectures, guided b
items.title_ar: AutoCompress: Automated Hardware-Guided Model Compression
items.summary_ar: تقدم الورقة AutoCompress وهو إطار لـ pruning لنماذج LLM يدمج قيود latency و throughput وGPU memory مباشرة في differentiable architecture search. يحسّن الإطار البنية العامة والطبقات بشكل مشترك لإنتاج architectures غير متجانسة. الفكرة الأساسية أن عدد المعاملات وحده لا يتنبأ بهذه المقاييس.
items.why_ar: يفيد المهندس عند نشر نماذج داخلية على عتاد محدود لأن الضغط يتم وفق قيود الخدمة الفعلية لا وفق عدد المعاملات.
items.title_en: AutoCompress: hardware-guided pruning for LLMs
items.summary_en: AutoCompress is a framework that folds latency, throughput, and GPU memory constraints directly into differentiable architecture search for LLM pruning. It jointly optimizes global and per-layer structure to produce heterogeneous architectures. The authors argue that parameter count alone does not predict these serving metrics.
items.why_en: It helps when deploying internal models under hardware and serving constraints rather than parameter budgets.

items.title: Fast and Exact Relative-Position Attention via Structure-Aware Kernels
items.snippet: Relative-position attention mechanisms offer compelling alternatives to RoPE across various transformer architectures, delivering superior performance in domains such as audio. These mechanisms typically modify attention scores by adding content-position or bias-position terms. Unlike RoPE, which encodes position via per-token rotations directly on the queries and keys, relative-position terms generally require pairwise offset-dependent computation or lookups, complicating their integration into fused attention kernels and introducing severe memory, bandwidth, and compute overheads as sequences scale. To address this bottleneck, we propose an exact attention algorithm that incorporates addit
items.title_ar: Fast and Exact Relative-Position Attention عبر kernels واعية بالبنية
items.summary_ar: تقترح الورقة خوارزمية attention دقيقة تدمج relative-position terms داخل fused attention kernels. الهدف تقليل تكلفة memory وbandwidth وcompute مع نمو طول الـ sequences. تقدم الورقة بديلاً عملياً لـ RoPE في transformer architectures.
items.why_ar: إذا كنت تبني transformer models أو تحسّن inference latency على sequences طويلة، فهذا يمس طبقة attention مباشرة.
items.title_en: Fast and Exact Relative-Position Attention via Structure-Aware Kernels
items.summary_en: The paper proposes an exact attention algorithm that integrates additive relative-position terms directly into fused attention kernels. It targets the memory, bandwidth, and compute overhead that grows with sequence length. The approach is presented as an efficient alternative to RoPE across transformer architectures.
items.why_en: If you build transformer models or optimize inference latency on long sequences, this touches the attention layer directly.

items.title_en: The Five Pillars of Trust for Agentic Commerce

items.title_en: SAOS-3624/dsh-see-now: Real-Time Screen Vision for AI

items.why_en: Its frame filtering and multi-frame packing idea can cut token costs for vision agents.

items.summary_ar: يقترح العنوان طريقة جديدة لتوليد النص بشكل متوازٍ وتدريجي من الخشن إلى الدقيق، بدلاً من التوليد التسلسلي. النص المتاح قصير ولا يقدم تفاصيل عن النتائج أو التقييم.

items.title_en: Next-Concept Modeling: Fast Parallel Coarse-to-Fine Text Generation
items.summary_en: The title proposes a method for generating text in parallel, moving from coarse to fine, instead of sequential decoding. The available text is minimal and gives no details on results or evaluation.
items.why_en: It may matter if you are exploring faster inference for text generation models in banking workloads.

items.title: Where to Connect? Boosting MLLMs via Dynamic Gated Pathways across ALL ViT and LLM Layers
items.snippet: A central yet under-explored question in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) is where to connect---how visual information from a hierarchical vision encoder should be wired into the layer-wise semantics of a large language model. Mainstream MLLMs inject a fixed single-layer visual representation into the LLM and treat all LLM layers as a single consumer, ignoring that different layers demand different visual granularities. Recent multi-layer fusion methods either compress hierarchical features on the encoder side or rely on predefined sparse or hierarchical layer-to-layer connections, and therefore stop short of modeling adaptive cross-layer interactions between the ViT and LLM hierarch
items.title_ar: أين يُربط الـ vision encoder؟ تحسين MLLMs عبر gated pathways
items.summary_ar: يطرح البحث سؤال أين يجب ربط المعلومات البصرية داخل LLM بدلاً من حقن طبقة بصرية واحدة ثابتة. يقترح Dynamic Gated Pathways تربط طبقات ViT وطبقات LLM بشكل تكيفي. الهدف تحسين أداء MLLMs عبر تفاعل أوسع بين المستويات.
items.why_ar: يقدم فكرة معمارية مفيدة لمن يبني أنظمة multimodal على أساس Vision Transformer و LLM.
items.title_en: Where to Connect? Dynamic Gated Pathways for MLLMs
items.summary_en: The paper studies how visual features from a hierarchical vision encoder should connect to layers of a large language model. It argues that fixed single-layer injection ignores varying visual granularity needs across layers. The proposed method uses dynamic gated pathways between ViT and LLM layers.
items.why_en: It offers an architectural idea useful if you design multimodal systems combining a ViT and an LLM.

items.title: parse_number() as a SQLite extension: C vs Rust
items.snippet: Research: parse_number() as a SQLite extension: C vs Rust I was out walking the dog when I got curious about how easy/difficult it would be to write a SQLite C extension that adds a parse_number() function for turning strings like -$1,234.56 or '12.5%' into numeric values that could be summed and sorted. I fired up regular Claude chat (Opus 5.5) and prompted : I'm thinking about a SQLite custom function 'parse_number(value)' that strips ',', '$', '£' and '%', handles a leading '-', and returns '
items.title_ar: دالة parse_number() كـ SQLite extension: مقارنة بين C وRust
items.summary_ar: يستعرض المقال كيفية كتابة SQLite extension يضيف دالة parse_number() لتحويل نصوص مثل -$1,234.56 و12.5% إلى قيم رقمية قابلة للجمع والترتيب. يقارن الكاتب تنفيذ الدالة بلغتي C وRust، وقد استعان بـ Claude في المسودة الأولى.
items.why_ar: يمكنك تجربة الفكرة خلال أيام لتنظيف بيانات مالية داخل قواعد SQLite المحلية.
items.title_en: parse_number() as a SQLite extension: C vs Rust
items.summary_en: The author explores writing a SQLite custom function parse_number() that strips currency symbols, commas, and percent signs and handles negative signs. He compares the implementation in C and Rust and used Claude Opus 5.5 to draft the initial prompt and code.
items.why_en: You can prototype this extension in a few days to clean financial string data inside SQLite.

items.title: Knowing When to Teach: Learning from Teachable Prefixes in Multilingual Reasoning Distillation
items.snippet: On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) improves reasoning by training a student on its own reasoning, using the same model conditioned on reference solutions as a teacher. Applying OPSD to multilingual reasoning requires the teacher to provide useful feedback across languages, even when the student makes mistakes in intermediate steps. We observe a phenomenon we call Teacher Drift: as these mistakes accumulate, the teacher may follow the student's incorrect steps instead of correcting them. Our analysis shows that this shift tends to occur earlier in lower-resource languages. To account for these differences across languages, we propose Teachable On-Policy Self-Distillation (TOPSD), which determ
items.title_ar: متى يجب التعليم: تحسين multilingual reasoning عبر distillation
items.summary_ar: يعالج البحث ظاهرة سماها الباحثون Teacher Drift، حيث يتبع المعلم أخطاء الطالب بدلاً من تصحيحها خلال On-Policy Self-Distillation. تظهر هذه الظاهرة مبكراً في اللغات الأقل موارداً. يقترح الفريق طريقة Teachable On-Policy Self-Distillation (TOPSD) لتحديد متى يكون التوجيه مفيداً.
items.why_ar: إذا كنت تبني أنظمة LLM تعمل بالعربية، فهذه المشكلة تنطبق مباشرة على جودة reasoning في اللغات الأقل موارداً.
items.title_en: When to Teach: Improving Multilingual Reasoning via Distillation
items.summary_en: The paper identifies Teacher Drift, where a teacher model follows a student's accumulated reasoning mistakes instead of correcting them during On-Policy Self-Distillation. The drift appears earlier in lower-resource languages. The authors propose TOPSD to decide when teacher guidance is useful.
items.why_en: If you build LLM systems for Arabic, this affects reasoning quality in lower-resource languages directly.

items.title: P^2-MOPD: Accelerating Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation via Parameter Priors
items.snippet: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation consolidates expert capabilities by supervising student-generated trajectories, whereas task arithmetic offers a training-free alternative through linear parameter combinations. We view the linear combination of student and expert parameters as a single differentiable model and propose P^2-MOPD, which jointly optimizes the mixing coefficients and the student weights under the same on-policy distillation objective. Unlike task arithmetic, which stays within the span of the frozen student and expert parameters for any choice of merging coefficients, P^2-MOPD keeps the student trainable, so the experts act as parameter priors without confining it to this spa
items.title_ar: P^2-MOPD: تسريع multi-teacher on-policy distillation عبر parameter priors
items.summary_ar: يقترح الباحثون P^2-MOPD لدمج أوزان الطالب والمعلمين الخبراء كنموذج واحد قابل للتفاضل. تُحسّن معاملات الدمج وأوزان الطالب معاً ضمن هدف on-policy distillation نفسه. يبقى الطالب قابلاً للتدريب، والمعلمون يعملون كـ parameter priors.
items.why_ar: يفيد إذا كنت تهتم بتقنيات distillation وتجميع قدرات عدة نماذج متخصصة في نموذج واحد.
items.title_en: P^2-MOPD: Accelerating Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation via Parameter Priors
items.summary_en: The paper combines student and expert parameters into one differentiable model and jointly optimizes mixing coefficients and student weights. Unlike task arithmetic, the student remains trainable beyond the span of merged parameters. The experts serve as parameter priors within the same on-policy distillation objective.
items.why_en: It is useful if you work on distillation or on consolidating multiple specialized models into one.

items.title: Learning to evolve by matching velocities
items.snippet: Learning the continuous-time evolution of nonlinear dynamical systems relies on trajectory-based objectives, which require simulating the learned dynamics during training and backpropagating through the numerical scheme, at a cost that grows with the rollout horizon. We show that trajectory-based objectives degenerate as the rollout horizon increases, hindering gradient-based optimization, and that the numerical scheme biases the learned dynamics by constraining the spectrum of the learned Jacobian to its absolute stability region. To overcome these limitations, we introduce Velocity Matching (VM), a simulation-free objective that relies on piecewise-linear interpolation and stochastic collo
items.title_ar: Velocity Matching: تعلم تطور الأنظمة الديناميكية بدون simulation
items.summary_ar: تعرض الورقة Velocity Matching، وهو objective لا يحتاج simulation أثناء التدريب ويعتمد على piecewise-linear interpolation. تشير إلى أن trajectory-based objectives تضعف مع زيادة rollout horizon. الهدف تحسين تعلم continuous-time dynamics.
items.why_ar: مفيد إذا كنت تنمذج أنظمة ديناميكية أو time-series forecasting ضمن مشاريع التنبؤ.
items.title_en: Learning to evolve by matching velocities
items.summary_en: The paper introduces Velocity Matching, a simulation-free objective based on piecewise-linear interpolation and stochastic collocation. It argues that trajectory-based objectives degrade as the rollout horizon grows. The aim is better learning of continuous-time nonlinear dynamics.
items.why_en: Useful if you model dynamical systems or time-series forecasting for prediction projects.
